3. The case of the plaintiffs, in brief, was that the land covered by C.S. khatian No.73 'of Mouza Silempur under P.S. Tanore, Rajshahi belonged to Shitol Sardar who died leaving behind 4 sons—Sadek Sardar, Safatullah Sardar, Farid Sardar and Shahatullah Sardar and they inherited the lands left by their father in equal share. Thereafter Safatullah Sardar died leaving 2 sons –Imanullah Sardar and Habib Sardar who inherited 1/4th share of their father. They took Tk.119/= as loan from the predecessor of the defendants namely Panaullah khan mortgaging the land they inherited from their father Safatllah Sardar on condition that they would refund the money within 7(seven) years with interest at the rate of Tk.2% to Panaullah Khan who in turn would return the mortgaged land to them, by executing and registering a mortgage deed on 10.6.1937. The plaintiffs were the successors of Imanullah Sardar and Habib Sardar. 

 8. Mr. Zaman Akhter, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners assailing the judgments and decrees passed by the Courts below submits that the predecessor of the plaintiffs, that is, Imanullah Sardar and Habib Sardar took loan of Tk. 119/- from Panaullah Khan, the predecessor of the defendants at the rate of 2% interest with a condition to re-pay within a period of 7(seven) years by executing and registering a deed of mortgage and delivered possession of the suit land. As they failed to re-pay the loan, the transaction was out and out a sale and past and closed. He further submits that S.A. and A.S. Khatian have been prepared in the name of the defendants which have a presumptive value. He also submits that the agreement being and a deed of transfer and as the period stipulated therein expired the suit was not maintainable as barred by limitation.
